sampling_model.units: The \(n=2m\) labeled units have fixed no-interference potential-outcome pairs summarized by \(R\in\mathcal R_0(n,K)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly \(m\) units receive treatment and \(m\) receive control.
sampling_model.overlap: Every labeled assignment in \(\mathcal Z_m\) has probability \(\binom{2m}{m}^{-1}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no estimated nuisance. Exact claims are uniform over the finite set \(\mathcal R_0(n,K)\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 3.1 characterizes invariant bijections for i.i.d. finite-support samples through equality of product probability masses.
Theorem 1 gives asymptotically conservative weak-null validity for a studentized Fisher randomization test on fixed finite populations.
Theorem 1 gives finite-sample level control for rank tests under an assumed finite-group invariance.
The paper constructs finite-sample exact confidence sets for the binary average treatment effect by prediction and randomization-test inversion.
Balanced binary exact confidence sets can be computed with \(O(n\log n)\) permutation tests, compared with \(O(n^2)\) generally.
Robustly studentized interacted OLS Fisher tests are finite-sample exact under the sharp null and asymptotically valid under the weak null.

body.tldr: Balanced complete randomization leaves the exact law under a weak average-effect null dependent on an unknown fixed response schedule. The proposal classifies the transformations that nevertheless preserve every such law. Binary outcomes retain every arm-transpose pair; three or more equally spaced levels destroy all nontrivial pairs except the two opposing endpoint-saturation profiles. The proof is certified by legal schedules with at most three heterogeneous units, and three are necessary in general. The induced maximal group makes conventional nonrandomized orbit-rank p-values take only the values \(1/2\) and \(1\), while an explicit corner p-value shows that this is not an impossibility claim for other exact tests.

project_justification.gap: Weak-null randomization theory supplies asymptotic studentization or exact inversion over compatible binary schedules, while general permutation theory assumes a null-invariant group. The literature does not identify the probability-equivalence partition induced by all fixed zero-average-effect schedules.
project_justification.niche: A finite outcome alphabet turns the missing-schedule problem into an exact multivariate-hypergeometric coefficient system whose common symmetries can be classified rather than assumed.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the complete alphabet-indexed equivalence frontier, the maximal common bijection group, and an optimal sparse-separator theorem, then states the resulting orbit-rank limitation with an explicit non-orbit exact counterexample.

body.related_work: \cite{WuDing2021} frames the weak-null obstacle through missing potential outcomes and obtains asymptotic control by studentization. \cite{HemerikGoeman2018} supplies the orbit-counting logic once a transformation group is known. \cite{DutzZhang2026} characterizes invariant bijections for i.i.d. finite-support samples, whose product-mass polynomial differs from the fixed-schedule hypergeometric kernel here. \cite{RigdonHudgens2015} and \cite{LiDing2016} construct exact binary average-effect confidence sets by compatible-table reasoning rather than a common group. \cite{AronowChangLopatto2025} proves a balanced computational acceleration for that inversion problem. \cite{ChungRomano2013} treats unequal group proportions through asymptotic multinomial--hypergeometric coupling. \cite{ZhaoDing2021} gives the robust-\(t\) weak-null workflow that motivates the applied audit, but its guarantee is asymptotic under the weak null.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The cubic endpoint identity and the two-heterogeneous-unit lower-bound case split remain proof obligations, not cited facts. An independent raw-assignment audit at \(K=3,n=6\) obtained counts \(1\) and \(0\) for the cubic witness and exhaustively confirmed equality under every legal schedule with at most two heterogeneous units. This finite check supports but does not prove the all-size theorem.
body.honest_scope: The headline concerns fixed no-interference schedules, balanced complete randomization, histogram-measurable common bijections, and equally spaced finite alphabets. It does not classify every exact weak-null test, validate a particular sharp-null permutation statistic, or cover covariate-adaptive, stratified, clustered, or unequal-arm designs. Under a diagonal sharp-null schedule, Proposition 1 reduces exactly to the familiar multivariate-hypergeometric law. Unequal allocation is retained as Open-ended Question 1 because treatment complementation no longer preserves the assignment space.
